analysis.summary: The PR refactors cart price conversion logic but introduces a functional regression where requested price types (Commercial vs. Private) will be ignored during cart refreshes due to scope removal in a shared utility.

bugs.title: Regression: Cart price type preference lost in refreshCart
bugs.description: The 'customerType' variable (representing Private vs. Commercial pricing) has been removed from the queryParams destructuring inside refreshCart. Although still present in the function signature and passed by callers, the variable is no longer in scope for the function body.
bugs.risk: Since refreshCart is responsible for building the cart response model, losing the customerType variable means downstream factory functions (like createCartModel) will receive undefined, causing the cart to display incorrect price formatting or values (e.g., defaulting to Private/Gross prices when Commercial/Net was requested).
bugs.codeSnippet:
-    customerType,
-    envName,
-    language,
...
+  const {awsRequestId, baseSiteId, cartId, envName, language, salesChannel} =
+    queryParams;

bugs.title: Invalid JSON stringification of staticVerifySecret
bugs.description: The staticVerifySecret option is being passed as a JSON-stringified object instead of a plain object. Most BFF middleware implementations expect a direct object configuration for secret verification.
bugs.risk: The middleware will likely fail to parse the configuration or fail to match incoming headers against a stringified JSON blob. This will result in 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden errors when the BFF attempts to verify the request or fetch endpoint configurations.

notBugs.reason: The logic to only trigger convertCartPrice for anonymous users is preserved from the previous implementation in refresh-cart.ts and is standard for this domain where logged-in user prices are controlled by backend account groups.
While userId was removed from the queryParams destructuring in refresh-cart.ts, it is safely replaced by auth.userId in the getCart call, which is populated correctly by the caller.
